item.title: Sagrada Familia got 24-tonne ‘glue job’ ahead of Gaudí’s centenary as world’s tallest church
item.description: The Sagrada Familia continues to rise with the aid of cutting-edge technology and unique adhesive solutions that bond stone with steel, reinforcing its many panels. This modern construction effort employs digital modeling and off-site prefabrication to expedite the building process, all while contending with environmental factors like salinity and underground vibrations. The ongoing project remains a testament to the spirit of innovation and teamwork in contemporary architecture.

item.title: Jacksonville donates 20 acres for $300M university campus and semiconductor research
item.description: Jacksonville is donating over twenty acres for a new University of Florida campus. This significant investment will support graduate programs and semiconductor research initiatives. The city's contribution totals one hundred million dollars towards the project. The wider UF Jacksonville project has attracted three hundred million dollars in investment. This new campus aims to develop talent and foster innovation in the region.

item.title: Lawsuit Seeks To Halt Border Work: Texas ranchers sue Trump plan; say Big Bend crossings are minimal
item.description: In a bold stand for their land and legacy, Texas landowners and conservationists are taking legal action against the Trump administration's border wall efforts. They emphasize that the Big Bend area, known for its natural beauty, has minimal illegal crossing incidents. The lawsuit contests the rationale behind sidelining environmental protections and raises alarms about potential harm to both private properties and local ecosystems.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Roosevelt took oath in a friend's library in 1901; 125 years later, the ceremony was reenacted
item.description: On September 14, 1901, Theodore Roosevelt became US president in the library of Ansley Wilcox’s Buffalo home after William McKinley died. For the 125th anniversary, the Theodore Roosevelt Inaugural Site recreate the ceremony in the same room. Actor Joe Wiegand portray Roosevelt, arriving in Buffalo by train before taking the 35-word presidential oath.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A 66-million-year-old gastropod fossil was found at a 5,000-year-old settlement in Ankara
item.description: A 66-million-year-old gastropod fossil was unearthed at an Ankara archaeological site. This ancient creature lived during the Tethys Sea's final phases. Researchers are investigating how the fossil arrived at the Kulhoyuk settlement. The discovery connects the site's history to a much older geological past. This finding offers insights into the region's ancient landscape and inhabitants.

item.title: Clementon Park site for sale: NJ park shuts after 119 years
item.description: Clementon Park and Splash World will close permanently after 119 years of operation. The New Jersey amusement park announced its difficult decision on September 9. The property is now up for sale, hoping for a buyer to preserve its legacy. IB Parks & Entertainment, the current owner, did not specify closure reasons. The park's final season will conclude in 2026.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Ohio community seeks 850 acres from coal company; forest could link 74,000 acres of public land
item.description: In Southeast Ohio, local stakeholders are actively pursuing the acquisition of former coal land to establish a new community forest aimed at linking Wayne National Forest with Strouds Run State Park. The envisioned Sugar Creek Community Forest will not only provide public access and recreational options, but also promote regenerative conservation and stimulate economic growth within the area.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Nathan, the Sydney gardener whose response to a homeless man's request for change went viral
item.description: Sydney gardener Nathan Stafford offered a homeless man named Robert a chance to earn money instead of simply giving him spare change. After helping Stafford clear leaves from a street in the rain, Robert received $100. Stafford, who has experienced homelessness himself, said he wanted to give Robert respect, dignity and a sense of purpose, and also arranged food and warm clothes for him.

item.title: UK farmer grows from 20 sheep on 18 acres to 200 sheep on 250 acres with solar grazing
item.description: Sheep grazing beneath solar panels provides farmers expanded land access. This innovative approach helps manage vegetation and reduces maintenance costs for solar farms. Hannah Thorogood, a sheep farmer, experienced significant flock growth due to this arrangement. Solar grazing offers a valuable opportunity for smaller and younger farmers facing land challenges. Combining renewable energy with agriculture creates a beneficial model for all involved.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Children in China trekked 3 hours up and down an 800m cliff to school; two elevators and a cable car cut it to 30 minutes
item.description: In Nizhuhe village, children can now travel to school efficiently and securely. A revolutionary new transport system has eliminated the previous risky three-hour journey along the cliffs. With the introduction of two elevators and a cable car, the village is seamlessly connected to the school. This modernization has not only made education accessible but has also sparked a boost in local tourism and economic growth.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet scientist Sethuraman Panchanathan, first Indian American to win Arthur M. Bueche Award
item.description: Sethuraman Panchanathan, an Indian American engineer and former NSF director, has been named the 2026 recipient of the National Academy of Engineering’s Arthur M. Bueche Award. He is the first Indian American and Arizonan to receive the honour, which recognises his work in science, technology policy, translational research and expanding opportunities nationwide.
